title: fix(objectql): report a refused write at `warn`, not `error` — the caller was already told
body:
Fixes #17052

Clause-②: no — this PR puts no new key on any published payload. It **narrows** what the three write doors claim at `error`; `writeFailureLogMeta()` is module-local and unexported, no name was added to any repo-wide list, and no schema, error code or accept set moved. Re-declared from the DELIVERED diff by the reviewing seat, not inherited from the claim. The `patch` grading below therefore stands.

`insert`, `update` and `delete` each end their `catch` with `throw e`, and logged
the failure at ERROR one statement earlier. AGENTS.md → *Degradation log levels*
names that exact shape and forbids it: **"a failure handed to the CALLER is not
a degradation at all … Do not bolt a `logger.error` onto such a site."** The
requester is told, on every path, by the loudest means available. The three
doors now report at `warn`, carrying the same diagnosis.

## ⭐ Zone 2 first: the premise, verified before anything was written

The ruling was hung on "the propagation checker can structurally prove **every**
path out of these catches delivers". Measured, both halves:

**The substance holds — every path delivers.** Each catch body's only exit is
the unconditional `throw e`; there is no branch, no early return, no loop. The
checker's own model agrees: in `catchDeliversFailure()`, `analyzeStmt` on a
`ThrowStatement` returns `{ delivered: true, terminates: true }` under the
comment *"A rethrow IS delivery — the loudest kind."* So the fork the dispatch
told me to stop for — *some path exits without telling the caller* — **did not
occur**, and shape 1 lands.

**The mechanism named in the ruling is unavailable, and that is measured, not
argued.** `FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES` cannot be used here. I probed it rather
than reasoning about it — added `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts::insert` to the
map, ran the gate, restored (restore verified by `git hash-object` against the
HEAD blob, `87a4b61… == 87a4b61…`):

```
✗ 1 stale entr(ies) in FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES — the declaration excuses nothing, so delete it
  packages/objectql/src/engine.ts::insert
GATE EXIT=1
```

Two independent structural reasons:

1. **The catch is never a seam of that rule.** `analyzeSourceFile`'s step 1
   (`collectGuardedCalls`) returns empty — the raw ObjectQL verbs are
   deliberately *not* in `DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES`, and the checker's own
   header says why (#12981: declaring them repo-wide drags in 36 quiet
   degradations). `--list` confirms it: of the log-level rule's 29 seams the
   only `engine.ts` entry is `syncSchema()@14484`.
2. **Even as a seam it would not attach.** `catchDeliversFailure()` requires
   `evidence` — a declared propagation *call*. A bare `throw e` leaves
   `evidence` undefined, so the function returns `undefined` and the site is
   excused by the **rethrow limb** (`propagatesAlways`), never by a declaration.

⇒ A declaration here is stale by construction and turns `pnpm
check:durability-log-level` red. ⛔ I did not weaken the checker to make it fit;
the correct reading is that the checker already proves delivery for this shape
by the route it reserves for rethrows. `pnpm check:durability-log-level` is
**green** on the delivered tree (29 seams, 63 self-test cases).

## ⛔ How I verified the two earlier rulings survived (#8682, #14095)

This is the part that nearly went wrong, and the trap is worth naming: **the
`Logger` contract gives an `Error` slot to `error`/`fatal` only.** `warn(message,
meta?)` has two parameters. And `Error.message`/`Error.stack` are
**non-enumerable**, so handing the error to `warn` as meta does not merely lose
the slot — it serialises `{}` and destroys the diagnosis one level down, which
is precisely the loss #14095 refused.

So the doors build the bag `ObjectLogger.write()` builds from the slot
(`{ …meta, error: { message, stack } }`), via a module-local
`writeFailureLogMeta()`. Measured against the **real** platform logger — before
(old `error` call) vs after (new `warn` call), plus the naive move as a negative
control:

```
BEFORE: …Z ERROR Insert operation failed {"object":"sys_oauth_resource","error":{"message":"UNIQUE constraint failed: doc.identifier [statement and bound values redacted]","stack":"Error: …\n    at Database.prepare (…)"}}
AFTER : …Z WARN  Insert operation failed {"object":"sys_oauth_resource","error":{"message":"UNIQUE constraint failed: doc.identifier [statement and bound values redacted]","stack":"Error: …\n    at Database.prepare (…)"}}
REMAINDER IDENTICAL (level word stripped): true

NAIVE  (Error handed to warn as meta) : {"object":"sys_oauth_resource","error":{}}
NAIVE2 (Error spread flat into meta)  : {"object":"sys_oauth_resource"}
diagnosis present in NAIVE2: false
```

- **#8682** — the redaction runs exactly where it did: the callers still pass
  `redactBoundStatement(...)`, and it is that result's `message`/`stack` that are
  read. The suite that pins it (`driver-fault-redaction.test.ts`) still asserts
  the failing column is named, and that neither field carries `SECRET`,
  `DESCRIPTION` or `insert into`.
- **#14095** — the entry still takes the `cause`, not the envelope: the choice
  of *which value* to hand in is unchanged at all three call sites, so MySQL's
  `for key 'crm_account.secret_note'` and the driver's own frames still arrive.
  Its suite (`engine-update-duplicate-record.test.ts`) reads the same two fields
  it always did, now out of `meta.error`.

## The sweep the card marked NOT MEASURED

AST matcher over `packages/objectql/src` (145 files carrying a `catch`),
following same-file helper calls one frame — the same visibility
`collectLoggedLevels()` has — and discriminating by **path**: an error log counts
only when it is on the same path as the rethrow.

| verdict | site |
|:--|:--|
| in class | `engine.ts:9710` → `Find operation failed` (via `reportFindFailure`) |
| in class | `engine.ts:11010` → `Insert operation failed` ⭐ positive control |
| in class | `engine.ts:12382` → `Update operation failed` ⭐ positive control |
| in class | `engine.ts:13832` → `Delete operation failed` |
| discriminated out | `hook-wrappers.ts:418` → logs at ERROR only on the branch that **suppresses** (`onError:'log'`, then `return`); its rethrow branch logs nothing |

**Positive control**: the matcher finds both sites the card established, by name.
**Negative control**: `hook-wrappers.ts` is a real ERROR-and-rethrow-in-one-catch
and is still classified out, so the path limb is exercised rather than vacuous —
and it is correct as it stands, because on the branch that logs, the caller is
*not* told.

**Repaired: 3 of 4** — `insert`, `update`, `delete`. The write doors are one
shape in one file, and `delete` is the same defect the card describes.

**Scoped out and filed: `find`.** Its level was set deliberately by a separate
ruling (`reportFindFailure`'s docblock weighs the driver's own surviving `warn`
against a second line) whose scope note explicitly reasoned about the write
verbs. Moving it is a decision, not a repair, so it is a card rather than a rider
— see `out_of_scope_findings`. Both stale prose rulings that would otherwise have
been left contradicting the code are corrected here: `reportFindFailure`'s
"`insert`/`update`/`delete` keep their unconditional `error`", and
`driver-fault-redaction.ts`'s specimen line and its "not to lower the level"
sentence (whose ⛔ was about *this exposure's* remedy and stays).

## Consumers surveyed before moving the level

Every mention of the three messages, repo-wide (29 hits, 18 files), classified:

**Depends on the level (4):**
- `scripts/publish-smoke.sh` — ⭐ the consumer that made this a release problem.
  `SMOKE_ERROR_LOG_PATTERN` fails a boot on any error-level line. Its own header
  rules the direction this change relies on: *"⛔ The severity is NOT the
  predicate. Widening the error scan to WARN is the obvious repair and it is the
  wrong one: warn is where this repo deliberately puts functional degradation …
  so a healthy boot HAS warn lines"*. So `warn` is the level this gate is built
  to tolerate, and no gate change is owed.
- `engine-strict-readonly-warning-truthful.test.ts` (⭐ positive control — the pin
  the dispatch named), `engine-find-missing-table-log-level.test.ts`,
  `driver-fault-redaction.test.ts`, `engine-update-duplicate-record.test.ts`.
  All four **moved, not deleted** — each now asserts the level the door takes,
  and three gained an assertion that nothing is emitted at `error` any more, so
  the move cannot be read as a copy.

**Does not depend on the level (7 runtime prose references):** `plugin-security`
(×4), `cli/src/utils/schema-migration-plugins.ts`, and two test comments all
point operators at *"the query engine's 'Insert operation failed' / 'Update
operation failed' entries"* — they name the **message**, never the level, so they
stay true. Verified by reading each string, not by grepping for a level word.

## Level choice: `warn`, not `debug`

The card allowed either. `debug` is refused by evidence, not taste:
`engine-find-missing-table-log-level.test.ts` already pinned that this line must
**not** land at `debug` (its `toHaveLength(0)` assertion is untouched by this PR
and still passes), and the platform default level is `info` — at `debug` the
diagnosis #8682 and #14095 fought to keep would be invisible in production,
which Zone 1 rule 4 forbids. `warn` keeps it on by default and off the channel
`publish-smoke` reads.

## Gates

62 derived families from `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, exit codes captured to
disk before any pipe, reconciled with `--ran`:
`✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 62 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.`

- **57 green**, including `check:durability-log-level` (the neighbouring gate the
  card asks about — it stays green, and its rule was never the one firing here:
  it fires on a catch logging *below* error *without* rethrowing, the opposite
  direction), `check:nul-bytes`, `check:published-files`, `check:doc-authoring`,
  `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-check-coverage`.
- **5 initially exit 3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET** (they read a built tree). After
  `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/objectql...' build`, three of them are **green**:
  `check:dts-closure` (78/78 declaration files across 15 built packages),
  `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`.
- **2 remain exit 3, and both want a WHOLE-TREE build** — `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`
  (47 more packages unbuilt) and `check:type-check-debt` (its `--re-measure` half
  needs 17 more dependency closures, and it refuses to measure a different world).
  Recorded NOT MEASURED — neither pass nor failure — and left to CI, which builds
  the farm.

### Tests — measured

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test` → **289/289 files, 4865/4865 tests
passing**. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` → **OK**.

⚠️ These took five acquisition windows: the container's shared heavy-verify lock
was held continuously by another seat's run (`issue-8772/final.sh`, pid 5749) for
~37 minutes, and four calls returned `VERDICT queue-timeout (exit 99) · never
acquired` before the lock freed. The place was kept via `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT`
throughout, and nothing was recorded as a red on the strength of an unacquired
lock.

**Running the WHOLE package rather than the message-matched files paid for
itself** — it found one consumer no grep could have reached, and two defects in
my own rig:

- `engine-delete-restricted-locale.test.ts` — #7307's pin that the delete door's
  `developerMessage` reaches the server log. It monkey-patches the logger method
  and reads the meta **by argument position**, so it never mentions `Delete
  operation failed` and the message survey could not see it. `warn(message, meta)`
  has no `Error` slot, so the meta moved from the third argument to the second.
  It now captures both levels and takes meta from the right position for each,
  which makes it a statement about the log rather than about one method.
- `engine-strict-readonly-warning-truthful.test.ts` — `warns` collected *every*
  warn-level message, so the door's entry turned each strip assertion into a
  count of 2. The message isolation this suite already performed in
  `stripLineLevels()` now backs `warns` too, which is where the strip assertions
  actually read. (This is the accessor half of the isolation its docblock always
  described.)
- `engine-write-failure-log-level.test.ts` — my new rig drove the delete door with
  an unrecognised `id` option, so the engine refused the call before the driver
  and the door logged nothing at all. Addressed through `where`, which is what
  #4371's own refusal message names.

## Changeset

`.changeset/engine-write-failure-log-level-warn.md`, `patch` — published
behaviour **does** move (the level is what an operator greps, and
`publish-smoke.sh` reads it structurally), so `skip-changeset` would have been
wrong. It states the FROM → TO for anyone grepping or alerting on these lines.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么** — `packages/objectql` 的三个写入门(`insert`/`update`/`delete`)在把失败抛回调用方之前打的那条日志,级别从 `error` 降到 `warn`;内容一个字节没动。

**为什么改** — AGENTS.md 明文规定:失败已经交给调用方的 `catch`,不算降级,不该挂 `logger.error`。代价是实测过的:全新项目第一次启动时,`@better-auth/oauth-provider` 用 UNIQUE 约束做竞态保护(它自己的文档就是这么写的),我们却在它 catch 之前先打了一条 ERROR,连续六次把 `publish-smoke / packed-tarballs` 刷红,而那个候选版本的探针全绿。

**风险与代价(含回滚)** — 风险集中在一处:`warn` 没有 `Error` 参数位,而 `Error` 的 `message`/`stack` 不可枚举,直接把错误对象塞进 meta 会静默变成 `{}`,#8682 和 #14095 两轮裁决保下来的诊断就没了。所以按 `ObjectLogger` 自己的拼法重建了那个字段,并用真实 logger 实测:除级别词外整行字节一致(负对照见上)。回滚成本低——单包单文件,三处调用点加一个模块内私有函数。已发布面只动了日志级别,changeset 里写清了 FROM → TO。

**席位意见** — (留空)

**你要做的** — 确认 `warn` 是这条线的终局级别(卡片允许 `warn` 或 `debug`,我按已有 pin 与默认日志级别选了 `warn`);以及 `find` 门的同类问题我按裁决另立卡而没有顺手改,请确认这个边界。
